blocks.value: When a company earns profits, it can either reinvest the money back into the business or share a portion of the profits with its shareholders. This payment is called a Dividend.

Imagine This: Four friends own a mango farm. After selling the harvest and paying all expenses, they decide to share part of the profit equally among themselves. That shared profit is similar to a dividend.
Not every company pays dividends. Fast-growing companies often reinvest profits to expand, while mature companies may regularly reward shareholders with dividends.
If a company declares a dividend of ₹10 per share and you own 100 shares, you will receive ₹1,000 before applicable taxes.
A company not paying dividends is not necessarily a bad company. It may be investing its profits for future growth.

blocks.question: What is a dividend?
choices: A portion of company profits shared with shareholders.
